facts.text: US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said that there should be 'no fear' and that 'everyone is safe' when discussing a nationwide air traffic outage.
BBC's Asma Khalid explains how the Nvidia affair could threaten US national security and risk sensitive US technology getting into China.

A Yahoo reporter who is currently on a plane on the tarmac waiting to depart on a United Airlines flight from Los Angeles International Airport says her pilot said, "In a nationwide ground stop, FAA just released an advisory, and we are told that at this time the ground stop will last until 11 p.m.
Tammy Duckworth, a Democrat from Illinois and a ranking member of an aviation subcommittee, called for an investigation into the nationwide groundstop.
"The safety of our skies is built on redundancies," she wrote on X in response to Duffy's update.
Mullin said that it would "take some time" for the issue to be resolved and that flights in the air were being dealt with on a "case-by-case" basis.

Airlines for America, an industry trade organization representing major U.S. airlines, wrote in a post on X , "Safety is always our top priority." It added that it's in communication with the Department of Transportation and the FAA.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters Friday evening that there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat is behind the communications outage affecting flights.
The pilot added, "What happened was a communications outage that started in Kansas City Center, which is responsible for the airspace above the middle of America, and it spread nationwide."

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has sought to reassure Americans that passengers remain safe as authorities investigate the unprecedented communications disruption behind Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop.
The comments came as Homeland Security received calls from concerned Americans asking whether the shutdown was connected to a terrorist attack.
Despite growing concerns about disruption to passengers and airlines, Mullin said officials could not yet estimate when the nationwide ground stop would end.

Much of the air traffic across the U.S. was shut down suddenly Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for all departing flights “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” The unusual alert, which was issued at 3:54 p.m.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was “no indication as of yet” that there was anything “nefarious” that caused the ground stop.
Airports could quickly become crowded with planes trying to land as the aircraft currently on the ground aren’t able to depart.
